text: After Ehud was dead, the Israelites again did what was evil in the sight of the LORD.
So the LORD sold them into the hand of Jabin king of Canaan, who reigned in Hazor. The commander of his army was Sisera, who lived in Harosheth-hagoyim.
Then the Israelites cried out to the LORD, for Sisera had nine hundred iron chariots, and for twenty years he had cruelly oppressed the Israelites.
Now Deborah, a prophetess, the wife of Lappidoth, was judging Israel at that time.
She used to sit under the Palm of Deborah between Ramah and Bethel in the hill country of Ephraim, and the Israelites came up to her for judgment.

She sent for Barak son of Abinoam from Kedesh in Naphtali and said to him, "Has not the LORD, the God of Israel, commanded you: 'Go, march to Mount Tabor and take with you ten thousand men from Naphtali and Zebulun.

versions.text: She sent for Barak son of Abinoam from Kedesh in Naphtali and said to him, "The LORD, the God of Israel, commands you: 'Go, march to Mount Tabor and take with you ten thousand men from Naphtali and Zebulun.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew uses the rhetorical question form הֲלֹא צִוָּה ("Has not ... commanded?"), which implies Barak already knows the command. The flattened statement loses this rebuke-like nuance, and the question reads well aloud.

text: I will draw out Sisera, the commander of Jabin's army, to meet you at the Kishon River with his chariots and his troops, and I will give him into your hand.'"
Barak said to her, "If you go with me, I will go; but if you will not go with me, I will not go."

"I will surely go with you," she said, "but the honor will not be yours on the road you are taking, for the LORD will sell Sisera into the hand of a woman." So Deborah rose and went with Barak to Kedesh.
Barak summoned Zebulun and Naphtali to Kedesh, and ten thousand men marched up behind him. Deborah went up with him as well.
Now Heber the Kenite had separated from the other Kenites, the descendants of Hobab, the father-in-law of Moses, and had pitched his tent by the oak at Zaanannim, near Kedesh.
When Sisera was told that Barak son of Abinoam had gone up Mount Tabor,
he summoned all his chariots, nine hundred iron chariots, and all the troops with him, from Harosheth-hagoyim to the Kishon River.

versions.text: he called out all his chariots, nine hundred iron chariots, and all the troops with him, from Harosheth-hagoyim to the Kishon River.
versions.explanation: "Summoned" matches the same verb (וַיַּזְעֵק) already rendered "summoned" in verse 10 and reads more naturally than "called out," which can be misread as "shouted."

text: Then Deborah said to Barak, "Up! This is the day the LORD has given Sisera into your hand. Has not the LORD gone out before you?" So Barak charged down from Mount Tabor with ten thousand men behind him.
And the LORD routed Sisera and all his chariots and all his army by the edge of the sword before Barak. Sisera got down from his chariot and fled on foot.

versions.text: And the LORD threw Sisera and all his chariots and all his army into a panic before the edge of Barak's sword. Sisera got down from his chariot and fled on foot.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has two distinct phrases: "by the edge of the sword" (לְפִי־חֶרֶב) and "before Barak" (לִפְנֵי בָרָק). The current rendering collapses them into "before the edge of Barak's sword," which is not what the text says and obscures that Barak is the one before whom the rout takes place.

text: Barak pursued the chariots and the army as far as Harosheth-hagoyim, and Sisera's whole army fell by the sword; not one man was left.
Meanwhile Sisera fled on foot to the tent of Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite, for there was peace between Jabin king of Hazor and the house of Heber the Kenite.
Jael came out to meet Sisera and said to him, "Turn aside, my lord, turn aside to me. Do not be afraid." So he turned aside to her in the tent, and she covered him with a blanket.
He said to her, "Please give me a little water to drink; I am thirsty." She opened a skin of milk, gave him a drink, and covered him again.
"Stand at the entrance of the tent," he told her, "and if anyone comes and asks you, 'Is there a man here?' say, 'No.'"
But Jael, Heber's wife, took a tent peg and a hammer in her hand, went quietly to him, and drove the peg through his temple into the ground while he lay fast asleep, exhausted. So he died.

Just then Barak came by in pursuit of Sisera, and Jael went out to meet him. "Come," she said, "I will show you the man you are looking for." He went in with her, and there lay Sisera, dead, with the tent peg through his temple.
On that day God subdued Jabin king of Canaan before the Israelites.
And the hand of the Israelites pressed harder and harder against Jabin king of Canaan until they destroyed him.
